ctor.rationale: `base(0, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Rare, TargetType.Self)` (Offering.cs:25-28) == cost 0 / SKILL / RARE / SELF.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new HpLossVar(6m)` + `new EnergyVar(2)` + `new CardsVar(3)` (Offering.cs:14-19) == all three numbers, all declared, so `base_hp_loss` and `magic_number` both report correctly.

OnPlay.rationale: All three steps and their order match: self-damage 6 (Unblockable | Unpowered | Move, Offering.cs:32) == `DamageCmd.deal(..., props=DamageProps.CARD_HP_LOSS)` -- through the full pipeline, so `on_damage_received` and Rupture fire, unlike card/breakthrough's hand-rolled loss -- then `PlayerCmd.GainEnergy(Energy.IntValue)` (33) == `EnergyCmd.gain`, then `CardPileCmd.Draw(Cards.BaseValue)` (34) == `DrawCmd.draw`. Presentation, folded in: the energy hover tip (23).

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Cards.UpgradeValueBy(2m)` (Offering.cs:39) == `self._cards += 2` (3 -> 5). Note the upgrade adds TWO and touches neither the HP loss nor the energy -- all three checked.

guards.what: the sim returns early on `if ctx.player.is_dead` after the 6 HP loss, skipping BOTH the energy and the draw (offering.py:41-42)
guards.issue: C# has no such early return: if the HP loss is lethal it still awaits the next command. DORMANT: the sim floors a death-prevented creature at 1 HP (cmds.py:106-112), so `is_dead` here means genuinely dead and the combat is lost on both sides before any listener could read the result. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/blood_wall's, card/bloodletting's and card/brand's guards (rule 3).
